text:
Nora: posted experiment mocks for billing list: group-by-org (rows grouped under org headers) vs flat-project-list. want quick takes on discoverability and billing scope.
Diego: link?
Nora: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/billing-grouping-experiment
Priya: org headers reduce cognitive load when companies have many projects, but they push recent invoices further down the page. mobile gets long.
Cole: flat-project-list is simpler for search but you lose context of which org the project belongs to. also hard to show org-level invoices.
Nora: question: where to place the download invoice CTA when grouped? inline per project row or on the org header for org-level invoices?
Priya: my vote: show download on rows, and an org header action for bulk downloads (month scope). keep primary actions local.
accessibility-bot: flagged: project rows use a stacked layout with no aria-labelledby for the org header — screen reader may not convey grouping.
Cole: also noticed the token denomination uses "M" and "k" shorthand. voiceover reads them weirdly. suggest aria-labels with full numbers and a visible tooltip for hover.
Diego: for metrics, propose AB: 30% grouped-by-org, 30% flat, 40% control. measure: invoice downloads per session, support mentions "missing invoice", average scroll depth, and bulk-download clicks.
Nora: will update mocks: add org-level bulk download CTA, aria-labelledby on grouped lists, and aria-label overrides on token shorthand. re-uploading in ~30m.
Priya: minor UX: when bulk download selected, show a confirmation toast with download progress and an option to email when ready. reduces accidental huge zips.
Cole: design nit: reduce header action size so it doesn't compete visually with org name. keep 48px tap target.
Nora: perfect. saving these notes for tomorrow's review. ping me for any urgent accessibility concerns. :thumbsup:
